speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health in relation to the mandatory tuberculosis screening exercise announced at three locations in Bedok on 30 April 2026, what lessons have been learned from this exercise for future reference, particularly in relation to its impact on the business prospects of high footfall locations such as hawker centres and markets.
This ensures that public health measures are coordinated with community engagement and that any concerns are addressed promptly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I refer to the notice that was released by CDC on 30 April where it said that the mandatory screening exercise would take place over three days, 4 to 7 May.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, does the Senior Minister of State not agree that in future, perhaps, a longer timeline for a screening exercise, or a differentiated regime for hawkers on the one hand and residents who may have transited through those areas where there is concern about a TB outbreak, could be considered?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Because that would reduce the anxiety faced by some of the hawkers, as the Senior Minister of State is aware.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: He was on the ground, I think, every day.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In that regard, you would also, in my view, have a more accurate reflection of the urgency of the problem and what is being done to resolve it.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: First, like I said in my earlier reply, CDA will have to do such precautionary screenings, in this case, for TB, on a regular basis, when needed.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is really part of our more proactive sentinel surveillance stance to minimise outbreaks of infectious diseases.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We do so when we believe there is a case where we can take early action, intervene early to prevent future outbreaks.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: When future outbreaks happen, the cost of doing so and cost of intervening will be much higher, especially for individuals and the community.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The second, I have explained and well, you can refer to my social media as well, I have done quite a fair bit.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And I am glad the Member has noted it when he came to visit me at Heartbeat@Bedok.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They frequented the place, perhaps had a meal or used some of the facilities.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Lastly, I just want to thank the Member for coming by at least a few times to my constituency to speak to my merchants, the hawkers, the residents.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And certainly, if that happens in Aljunied, I will make sure my colleagues will make sure that we will also return the favour, to show care and concern for residents.
